title: New Dundee Road housing and basic income advocacy
subtitle: Pinnacle Drive redesign, 1027 King Street East demolition notice, transit-area planning deferrals, surplus land framework, Eastwood neighbourhood plan
overview: Council approved a townhouse development at 404-430 New Dundee Road {{vote:m1}} despite resident concerns about traffic, grading and school capacity. It also approved a rezoning at 448 New Dundee Road and a revised, higher-unit-count but lower-profile design for 86 Pinnacle Drive after the developer reworked it with neighbours.

Council asked the federal and provincial governments to work toward an income-tested guaranteed livable basic income {{vote:m4}}. A proposed amendment to soften the wording lost on a tie. Council also received a notice to demolish the Art Deco building at 1027 King Street East, which lets the notice period run and allows a demolition permit as early as March 16, 2024.

Decisions on the Protected Major Transit Station Area planning framework and on inclusionary zoning were deferred to a March 18, 2024 special meeting so staff can talk further with people who made submissions. Council also adopted a City-owned land disposition framework, a new honorarium policy for advisory committee members, and an updated emergency management by-law. The meeting opened with a presentation from the Eastwood Neighbourhood Association on its neighbourhood action plan.

decisions.detail: Council adopted the Official Plan amendment and approved the zoning change for a Klondike Homes townhouse development, adopted its urban design brief, and ruled out further public notice.
Council approved the zoning by-law amendment for Hayre Properties Inc. and endorsed the urban design brief to be applied through site plan approval.
Council approved the amended zoning by-law and directed staff to generally follow the revised concept of two-storey stacked townhomes and semi-detached-style units at site plan.
Council received the notice of intention to demolish and let the notice period run its course, rather than pursuing heritage designation.
Council asked Canada and Ontario to work together to establish an income-tested guaranteed livable basic income, and to send the resolution to federal, provincial and municipal bodies.
Council deferred the Official Plan and zoning amendments for seven protected major transit station areas to the March 18, 2024 special meeting.
Council deferred the inclusionary zoning Official Plan and zoning amendments to March 18, 2024, to be considered alongside the transit station area framework.
Council adopted a framework to guide the sale and acquisition of surplus City land and directed staff to manage it as an asset portfolio.

debate: Residents who spoke on New Dundee Road raised concerns about traffic on a busy regional road, long left-turn waits, school capacity, parking, tree loss, density above the base zoning, and grading and retaining walls near existing homes. They asked for a deferral.

Staff said the Region reviewed and signed off on the traffic study, with a left-turn lane and a roundabout planned, and that engineers must certify the retaining wall. Staff added that the applications were past their decision deadline, so a deferral risked an Ontario Land Tribunal appeal. One councillor still wanted to talk to the Region about road widening and safety before deciding.

On 1027 King Street East, the applicant's heritage consultant and staff said the Art Deco section is structurally unsound and cannot be kept without bracing that would change its look. Councillors pressed on alternatives and asked for 3D documentation, and the developer agreed to explore it.

On basic income, a delegate argued it would reduce poverty and health costs and is affordable. Supporters cited pilot results and the needs of low-wage workers. Others worried about cost, the limited data, and whether a city resolution has any effect. The amendment to "research and consider" failed {{vote:m5}}.

At 86 Pinnacle Drive, the revised design drew praise from councillors and residents for lower heights, central parking and more units. One heritage-area resident asked for extra landscaping and screening at site plan.
